summary.text:
The task is to judge the exact glossary BOOK ENTRY for "Meat" against the strongest specific alternative, using the chapter as evidence.
The BOOK ENTRY is the best explanation of the supplied scriptural evidence.

The core identification—that “meat” is the word obeyed to completeness, while “milk” is the word received—directly accounts for the full range of references without contradiction. John 4:34 equates meat with doing the Father’s will; Matthew 12 50 and Luke 8:21 equate that will with hearing and doing the word; Psalm 40:8 shows the same will already written on the heart. Hebrews 5:14 then supplies the test: the mature believer’s senses are exercised precisely by carrying the received word through to obedience, so that good and evil can be discerned. Job 34:3 and John 7:17 close the loop: tasting and doing the word are the same act. John 6:55 (“my flesh is meat indeed”) and Matthew 24:45 (“meat in due season”) fit the same pattern once the word is embodied and carried to completion.

The common interpretation—that meat is advanced or mature teaching in contrast to milk as elementary doctrine—treats the two terms as labels for different levels of content.

support_scope.description: Support for the exact glossary BOOK ENTRY only, never for the supporting chapter as a whole.

book_secondary_elaborations.description: Secondary assertions actually printed in the glossary BOOK ENTRY; exclude chapter-only claims.

unsupported_glossary_assertions.description: Material assertions actually printed in the BOOK ENTRY that the evidence does not support. Must be empty for FULL and nonempty for CORE_ONLY.

chapter_only_objections.description: Objections to applications or arguments found only in the supporting chapter. Preserved for later chapter review and excluded from the glossary scope ruling.
